block_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

Eight CRITICAL vulnerabilities across four distinct packages are present, all with available fixes. Three findings represent duplicate CVEs across related packages: CVE-2021-3711 affects OpenSSL/libssl (EPSS 0.878), CVE-2022-29155 affects LDAP libraries (EPSS 0.699), and CVE-2020-15999 affects FreeType (EPSS 0.506, KEV-listed). A fourth distinct issue, CVE-2023-38408 in OpenSSH (EPSS 0.768), also has a fix available. All vulnerabilities are patchable with no known exploits in the wild except FreeType.

**Recommended Action:** Approve the build with a mandatory follow-up to upgrade all four packages to patched versions before production deployment. Prioritize OpenSSL and OpenSSH updates first due to higher EPSS scores and attack surface; FreeType should be included despite lower EPSS due to KEV listing.
review_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

All 20 findings are HIGH severity with fixes available and none are on the KEV catalog, indicating manageable risk. The vulnerabilities cluster around six distinct CVEs affecting core system libraries: HTTP/2 (libnghttp2), DNS resolution (libunbound), image processing (libwebp across 4 packages), OpenSSL/TLS (3 packages), Git, glibc, and LDAP. Most EPSS scores exceed 0.88, reflecting genuine exploitability, but the presence of available patches significantly reduces urgency.

**Recommended Action:** Approve this build with a scheduled patch window within 30 days targeting the highest-impact packages (OpenSSL, glibc, libwebp). Prioritize OpenSSL and glibc updates first due to their foundational role in the system; the others can be batched. Document the deferral and track completion to closure.
